A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same paper with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Corresponding material can be matched reliably despite pagination and layout shifts.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM attention-layer replacement experiments, FMNIST training results, and synthetic convergence experiments in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v4 reports original LLM attention-layer replacement experiments, FMNIST training results, and synthetic convergence experiments in Section 5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, bivector exponentiation, and the generalized two-rotor construction remain unchanged. The revised Spin-group definition changes the formal specification; both versions already construct rotors from bivector exponentials.

E1.justification: Both versions use Wikitext2, C4, PTB, ARC Challenge, HellaSwag, FMNIST, and the same synthetic rotation scenario. Appendix experiments are retained without changing dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding LLM comparisons retain LR1, LR4, BH1, and the original dense-model reference. The dense MLP comparator in the FMNIST experiment is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The model configurations, attention-layer replacement procedures, MSE fitting, evaluation metrics, and FMNIST setup are unchanged. Appendix C and Tables 5–6 retain the same experimental settings.

E4.justification: The layer-combination comparisons, width/depth analysis in Figure 5, and convergence analysis in Figure 6 are retained. Figure 6 moves pages without introducing a new analysis.

E5.justification: Figure 6 retains averaging over 50 runs and one-standard-deviation error bars. The averaging descriptions in Tables 1 and 11 and the checklist's statement that accuracy error bars are omitted are unchanged.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical results and parameter counts in Tables 1–4 and 7–11 are unchanged, as are the curves and findings in Figures 5–6. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds the requirement that r v r† remain in the vector subspace for every vector v to the Spin-group definition. Appendix B.3, Property 3 adds a grade-block-diagonal restriction and corresponding proof steps, including revised reasoning about unit-versor membership. These are localized formal revisions; the algorithm and parameter-count theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about compact bivector-based composition, differentiable rotor construction, and competitive downstream performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of performance, parameter efficiency, convergence, and computational limitations are unchanged. Grade preservation already motivates mixing across grades in v3; its explicit addition to the formal characterization does not introduce a new mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and computation-time disclosures. Code-access information is unchanged; displaced training-detail passages remain present.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to earlier composition, structured-layer, and geometric-algebra research are unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix B.3 gains a short grade-preservation explanation and localized revisions to the proof and concluding wording. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is repositioned within Section 3, and surrounding text reflows. Figure 6 moves from page 31 to page 32, shifting Table 7 downward; the figures and tables retain their content and display structure.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses an omitted vector-preservation condition in the Spin-group definition and explicitly incorporates grade preservation into Property 3 and its argument. This provides a limited improvement in mathematical specification and consistency with the existing structural analysis. The method, empirical support, reproducibility information, and practical limitations remain unchanged.
